title: The Structure of DNA
about: who found it, when, and where the work was done. Include several specific numbers, dates or names where the topic has them, some exact and some rounded or hedged (about, nearly, more than, up to).
passages: DNA is the MOLECULE that carries the instructions for building every living thing. In 1953, James Watson and Francis Crick worked out its shape at the Cavendish Laboratory in Cambridge, England, a university town where people have studied for more than 800 years. Watson was only 24, and Crick was 36. They showed that DNA is a double HELIX, like a ladder twisted into a spiral. On 25 April 1953, they shared their idea in the journal Nature, in a paper of a little over one page. According to Watson, Crick celebrated at a nearby pub called The Eagle.

Their discovery depended on the work of others. About 80 kilometers away, at King's College London, Rosalind Franklin used X-ray CRYSTALLOGRAPHY to make pictures of DNA. In May 1952, she and her student Raymond Gosling captured a famous image called Photo 51, which showed a clear X shape. Maurice Wilkins, who also worked at King's, showed it to Watson in early 1953 without asking her. In 1962, Watson, Crick and Wilkins won the Nobel Prize. Franklin could not share it, because she had died in 1958, when she was just 37 years old.
